<!-- pr-reviewer: 8f0a6d1b8bdda119cb9e8450b36e0f6234381458 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`: merges at the cut, after its parent #522). Reviewed only commit 8f0a6d1b; the other six commits are #522's.

**What looks good**
- The change is minimal: one flag line plus a comment in `assets/posts/haas.cps`, the refusal text in `crates/post/src/post/invert.rs:332` now reads "Fanuc and Haas", and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` matches. No new code runs in the post.
- Safety argument checked by reading `haas.cps` lines 440-545 against the mirror in `invert.rs` (touch target, trip, back-off delta, found expected, guard `to`). Every probing word is in the controller's frame:
  - `G31` takes the already-mirrored target.
  - The trip is read from `#5061-#5063`, which are work-frame skip positions, so they are negated on an inverted axis like the target.
  - The no-contact and guard alarms compare `#506x` to the same mirrored target.
  - The back-off is an incremental `G91 G1` with the mirrored delta.
  - The deviation is `mean - expected`, with the expected value mirrored.
  - `G10 L2 X[#5221+#190]` writes the register in the controller's frame, where the datum is negated too, so the written value is the physical correction. It is the same structure Fanuc already uses under #465.
- The numerics are pinned, not trusted. `inverted_probe` runs the real post output on a macro-B interpreter that simulates the machine (offset register holds the negated datum, skip position is negated):
  - every probe mode (face -Z/-X, edge -Y, corners, bore, boss) on standard, X-, Y- and XY-inverted machines, for both Fanuc and Haas;
  - G55 equals the physical datum, with a shifted part and with an unshifted one;
  - a part out of reach alarms `#3000=2` and writes nothing;
  - out of tolerance alarms `#3000=1`;
  - undoing any one of the touch target, back-off delta or found expected breaks the result (including the "no contact" alarm for the touch target), so the mirror is load-bearing.
- A probe toward +X on an X-inverted machine goes through the same corner cases (`corner +X+Y`): the mirrored target gives a travel of the opposite sign, and the trip read and the offset write come out physical.
- Non-inverted output is byte-identical (`an_uninverted_program_is_unchanged_by_the_flag`, over every case for both posts).
- The refusal without the flag is pinned by name on the shipped Haas and Fanuc scripts with the flag stripped (`probing_through_an_unverified_script_still_refuses_by_name`).
- The decision record `docs/decisions/392-haas-probe-inverted.md` is present and explains what was dropped. The body ends `Fixes #392` and has a `Changelog:` line. No snapshot, golden, `build.rs`, `.github` or dependency changes.

**Local results** (PR head, trial merge with `upstream/main` was already up to date, `MERGEABLE`)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| inverted_probe | 9 passed |
| inverted_post | 15 passed |
| probe_dialects | 13 passed |
| probe_op | 11 passed |
| conformance / fanuc_post / golden_cl / inverted_equivalence / posting / axis_direction | 6 / 11 / 23 / 2 / 17 / 12 passed |
| camcraft-post (all targets) | all passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

`probe_search` does not exist as a test binary in the tree, so it was not run.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- This is verified on a simulated inverted machine, as the PR says; no real Haas with an inverted axis was exercised. The simulator models `#5061-#5063` and `#5221+` as work-frame values negated on an inverted axis, the same assumption Fanuc made in #465, so a real-control check would be worth doing when one is available.
- I did not confirm that the `inverted_probe` fixtures emit `Guard` records (`haas.cps` `onProbeGuard`, `#3000=3`). The mirror of `Guard.to` is in `invert.rs:257`, and the guard compares against the same mirrored target as the touches, so it reads as correct. Worth a one-line pin if a guard case isn't already in the fixtures.
- `inverted_probe.rs` is at exactly 400 lines: do not grow it; split before adding cases.
- The review stacks on #522, so the merge order is #522 first, then this PR (retarget per Issue Law if needed).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
